hits.name: Codie_Sanchez
hits.text:
Before I was even pregnant, I asked my mom & dad for advice from raising me and my brother...

This is what they told me, maybe you'll find it useful too:

1. Your kids are not your friends. They’re yours to safeguard and support, but set rules. Biggest problem with most kids in our generation, their parents wanted to be liked not respected.

2. Psy ops are underrated. My mom had this line for whenever I got into trouble. She’d say, “When I ask you a question like this, I already know the answer. I am giving you a chance to come clean...” At which point I’d sing like a canary because I’m a scaredy cat. I found out today she rarely knew the answers. Brilliant and maniacal.

3. Always on the same page. My mom and dad rarely fought in front of my brother and I. They would never go back on the word of the other. United front to deal with us mini terrorists.

4. Make time. My dad had this silly line that is actually not silly: “You can make money, you can make a cake, but you can’t make time.” So they made allllll the time for us.

5. Four chairs. We have these four chairs in our living room, no tv. Growing up, we’d sit and debate and talk for hours. Politics. Opinions. Our days. Only thing not allowed was an opinion you couldn’t defend unemotionally. We still do this today.

6. Mi Sangre mi siempre. They’d always say, blood comes first. They meant it. I hired my brother, my dad, my mom, my cousin at times. We stick together and we may fight like hell but never in front of others.

7. Once you decide, you don’t quit. We could play any sport or instrument BUT if we committed we had to play the full year all out. No 3 lessons and quit. Taught us to choose thoughtfully and keep going even when it hurt.

8. Always call. They still pick up the phone nearly every time it’s family. My dad in a meeting will pause to answer my mom. My husband taught me this too, and I try to do the same. If they’re your first priority this is an easy way to prove it.

9. You’re not a princess, you’re a president. My dad always used to say that line. He told me this week that I lived up to it. Gutted me. He taught us we didn’t need to be saved, instead we could save ourselves and help others.

10. Hug often and seriously. If you’ve ever hugged my parents, they mean it when they do it. Such a simple, free gesture. My mom always gives you a hug and says vaya con dios... go with God. How can you not do big things with parents that hold you like that?

Just some lessons from parents I happen to think are some of the best in the world.

Moms & dads everywhere, I'm in awe of you.

Hardest job I've ever seen.

Hope I'm half as good at it as my parents were with us.
hits.hook: Before I was even pregnant, I asked my mom & dad for advice from raising me and my brother...

hits.draft_en:
Pick one craft.
Give it ten years.

Most people switch in year two.
By year five, the room is nearly empty.

That empty room is your unfair advantage.
hits.video_tip: Walk-and-talk, handheld, 10s. Open on an empty room or studio, walk in on 'that empty room'. No music, natural sound.

hits.name: JamesClear
hits.text:
Writing is the superpower of humankind. It is our truest form of magic. 

Writing allows you to conjure up something of value where nothing previously existed. It costs little for you to write down the lessons of your life and yet those few minutes spent writing can be life-altering for the right reader. As I once saw it put: "there is someone out there with a wound in the exact shape of your words."  

Furthermore, writing is the foundation of nearly every technology and innovation because we have to record what we know before we can build upon it. And these innovations are passed down from generation to generation, allowing our children to inherit a richer intellectual fortune than what we were born into. The world is richer because we write and nobody is made poorer in the process.
hits.hook: Writing is the superpower of humankind. It is our truest form of magic.

virals.name: tylermwebb
virals.text:
Steal like an artist. 

Author @austinkleon popularized this idea in 2012, when he argued that nothing is completely original and that the best artists: 

‣ Study
‣ Transform
‣ Remix

They use the work of multiple influences to create something new. And if you start looking, you'll see this all over the internet. 

One of my favorite examples is YouTuber Mr. Manny, who basically just took the concept of the old TV show 'Cops' and repackaged it for YouTube (I Spent 24 Hours with X).

Personally, I'd love to see someone recreate ESPN's 'Sports Science' for the internet.

virals.name: iasonioannis
virals.text:
This story about Pablo Picasso robbing innocent Africans helped me write an ad for a 9-figure brand that’s on track to spend 7 figures…

And it will make YOU a better Creative Strategist today than you were yesterday (2-minute read):

Most people see Picasso as the poster boy for originality…

But the reality is a little different.

Because all he did was take African art…

Rip their visual style…

And instead of sculpting statues like the Africans…

He put it into paintings while targeting a different audience (the West)...

And now the total valuation of the Picasso estate is estimated to be between $6 billion and $10 billion.

It’s the same approach I used on that winning ad.

All I did was:

1.  Swipe the structure of a winning ad in an adjacent niche

2.  Reword a couple of things + tweak the mechanism to fit my brand’s ingredients

3.  Change the on-screen UGC actor to a black girl instead of a white girl (targeting a different audience)

And boom.

It already spent over $500k and is now on track for 7 figures according to my head of creative [proof below]...

While stealing even more shamelessly than Picasso since I kept the visual the same (UGC creator in the kitchen).

So be like Picasso…

And steal like an artist.

- Iason (#1 Ad Bro)

P.S. Another thing I learned from Picasso is:

You don’t need more original ideas…

You need better places to steal them from…

More on this in my next post.

P.S.S.
